project.name: godkit
project.description: One shared harness for every AI agent. Godkit puts a committed .agent/ directory in a repo - board, thread, map, sprints, tasks, logs - and teaches Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Antigravity to read it before editing and write to it before finishing, so work is not redone and two agents never edit one file. A zero-dependency Node CLI plus sixteen skills, published as @codeforfee/godkit. The CLI owns only what a machine can decide; everywhere judgment starts, it stops and hands off to a skill.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Generated Claude-facing copy of AGENTS.md. It carries the full shared-state and file-ownership protocol so Claude sessions receive it without relying on hooks alone; edit AGENTS.md and regenerate instead of changing this file.

nodes.name: gemini-extension.json
nodes.summary: Antigravity/Gemini extension manifest. It exposes the packaged skills and agents directories and selects AGENTS.md as the extension context file.

nodes.name: godkit.md
nodes.summary: Generated Antigravity-facing copy of the canonical AGENTS.md protocol. It is byte-for-byte rule content for a host with no hook enforcement, so changes belong in AGENTS.md and the sync generator.

nodes.name: marketplace.json
nodes.summary: Claude plugin marketplace entry for the local godkit package, including owner metadata, description, category, and local source root.

nodes.name: plugin.json
nodes.summary: Claude Code plugin manifest. It publishes the godkit package identity and points Claude at the shared hook registry rather than duplicating hook definitions.

nodes.name: plugin.json
nodes.summary: Codex plugin manifest exposing the package's shared skills, agents, and hook registry. Keeping these as paths makes Codex consume the same canonical assets as the other hosts.

nodes.name: copilot-instructions.md
nodes.summary: Generated GitHub Copilot-facing copy of the canonical AGENTS.md collaboration rules. It exists as a host adapter and must be regenerated from AGENTS.md rather than edited independently.

nodes.name: architect.md
nodes.summary: Prompt contract for the architecture synthesis pass after batch graphs are merged. It derives project metadata, 3-8 named layers, and a 5-9 step start-here tour without inventing framework or runtime claims.

nodes.name: file-analyzer.md
nodes.summary: Prompt and schema contract for turning one scan batch into graph nodes and observed edges. It requires every assigned file to be read, stable relative-path IDs, actionable summaries, no guessed relationships, and exactly one scratch JSON output.

nodes.name: scan.js
nodes.summary: Deterministic filesystem scanner that categorizes authored files, applies hard skips plus a documented subset of .agentignore/.gitignore, and regex-extracts resolvable relative imports. Unknown types and files over 400 KiB are intentionally absent from the map input.

nodes.name: scan
nodes.summary: Walks a root in stable path order, skips unreadable or ignored entries, reads code to resolve internal imports, and returns file/category/size/line metadata plus language counts. Absolute paths are removed unless keepAbs is explicitly requested.

nodes.name: batch.js
nodes.summary: Greedy deterministic clusterer for semantic-analysis calls. It favors import-connected files, then same-directory neighbors, under a 60 KiB budget while guaranteeing every non-data file is placed once even when one file exceeds budget.

nodes.name: batch
nodes.summary: Builds stable analysis batches by traversing undirected import adjacency before filling with directory neighbors. Oversized seeds are retained rather than dropped, preserving full scan coverage.

nodes.name: graph.js
nodes.summary: Persistence and projection layer for project memory: guarded graph loading, portable path sanitization, node/edge normalization, saving, structural signatures, and generated MAP.md rendering. Node IDs are identity, duplicate nodes resolve last-wins, and dangling edges are dropped.

nodes.name: loadGraph
nodes.summary: Loads an existing graph but refuses to turn a nonempty malformed or graph-shaped-invalid file into an empty result. This guard prevents a parse failure from silently resetting committed project memory.

nodes.name: normalize
nodes.summary: Sanitizes node paths and complexity, deduplicates nodes by ID with last-write-wins semantics, deduplicates typed edges, drops dangling endpoints, and filters layer/tour references to known nodes.

nodes.name: saveGraph
nodes.summary: Normalizes a graph, creates the destination directory, and writes the canonical pretty-printed graph JSON. All callers receive the cleaned in-memory value that was persisted.

nodes.name: renderMap
nodes.summary: Projects graph metadata, architecture layers, and the ordered start-here tour into generated Markdown, then appends recall instructions that tell later agents to grep the graph rather than load it whole.

nodes.name: freshness.test.js
nodes.summary: Unit tests for rebuild classification thresholds, top-level path normalization, human freshness summaries, and exclusion of .agent from staleness checks. They exercise classify directly but do not create git repositories to cover staleness command failures.

nodes.name: godkit-doubt.toml
nodes.summary: Command adapter that forwards arguments to the godkit-doubt skill for pressure-testing a decision before it is recorded on the board.

nodes.name: godkit-evolve.toml
nodes.summary: Command adapter that forwards arguments to godkit-evolve for capturing, deriving, or repairing project-owned skills under .agent/skills.

nodes.name: godkit-execute.toml
nodes.summary: Command adapter that invokes the five-stage godkit-execute pipeline and passes through the requested plan or execution context.

nodes.name: godkit-frontend.toml
nodes.summary: Command adapter for the godkit-frontend design-taste skill, forwarding UI context and arguments to its visual direction workflow.

nodes.name: godkit-git.toml
nodes.summary: Command adapter for parallel-agent git mechanics, including worktrees, commit checkpoints, and shared .agent merges.

nodes.name: godkit-handoff.toml
nodes.summary: Command adapter for clock-in, scope claiming, and evidence-bearing clock-out through the godkit-handoff skill.

nodes.name: godkit-help.toml
nodes.summary: Argument-free command adapter that asks godkit-help to display the shared-state layout, ladders, skills, and CLI reference card.

nodes.name: godkit-lazy.toml
nodes.summary: Command adapter that passes the requested lite, full, ultra, or off intensity to godkit-lazy, including mode switching and reporting.

nodes.name: godkit-map.toml
nodes.summary: Command adapter that directs godkit-map to build or incrementally refresh graph.json and MAP.md with any caller-supplied scope.

nodes.name: godkit-output-enforcement.toml
nodes.summary: Command adapter for locking deliverable counts and rejecting placeholder or truncated output through godkit-output-enforcement.

nodes.name: godkit-plan.toml
nodes.summary: Command adapter that asks godkit-plan to split work on file boundaries, assign owners, and write the resulting task files.

nodes.name: godkit-review.toml
nodes.summary: Command adapter for reviewing orchestration quality or diagnosing a failed multi-agent run with godkit-review.

nodes.name: godkit-test.toml
nodes.summary: Command adapter for defining verification and the smallest regression check that proves requested behavior through godkit-test.

nodes.name: godkit.toml
nodes.summary: Top-level arrival command adapter: load shared state, refresh a stale map, synthesize and split the task, then claim scope before handling forwarded arguments.

nodes.name: lazy.js
nodes.summary: Centralizes lazy-mode configuration, runtime state, host-specific hook output, and instruction loading. Runtime mode is stored in one host-wide .godkit-lazy-active file, so concurrent sessions currently share and overwrite the same state.

nodes.name: isDeactivationCommand
nodes.summary: Recognizes only whole-message lazy-mode shutdown phrases, avoiding accidental deactivation when ordinary prompts merely mention normal mode.

nodes.name: configPath
nodes.summary: Returns the cross-platform Godkit config.json path used by both lazy and evolve settings.

nodes.name: getDefaultMode
nodes.summary: Resolves the default lazy intensity from GODKIT_LAZY_MODE, persisted config, then full.

nodes.name: writeDefaultMode
nodes.summary: Persists a validated defaultMode while retaining other parsed config keys; malformed config currently falls back to an empty object and is overwritten non-atomically.

nodes.name: statePath
nodes.summary: Selects the single runtime flag under Codex PLUGIN_DATA or the Claude config directory; it is host-scoped rather than session-scoped.

nodes.name: setMode
nodes.summary: Writes the active lazy intensity into the shared runtime flag.

nodes.name: clearMode
nodes.summary: Deletes the shared lazy runtime flag and treats absence as already off.

nodes.name: readMode
nodes.summary: Reads and validates the currently active intensity from the shared runtime flag; missing or invalid state is inactive.

nodes.name: writeHookOutput
nodes.summary: Serializes injected lazy context in the shape expected by Codex or Claude hook events, with raw stdout reserved for Claude SessionStart.

nodes.name: getLazyInstructions
nodes.summary: Loads the shipped lazy skill, removes frontmatter, keeps only the requested intensity row, and falls back to a compact built-in instruction if the skill file is unavailable.

nodes.name: sync-rules.js
nodes.summary: Generates every host's always-on rule file from AGENTS.md, adding Cursor frontmatter only where required. --check turns the same projection into a CI drift detector.

nodes.name: build
nodes.summary: Builds a rule copy, optionally prefixing Cursor's generated .mdc frontmatter.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Compares or rewrites four host rule targets from the canonical AGENTS.md body and fails CI with actionable drift output in check mode.

nodes.name: brandkit.md
nodes.summary: Image-only workflow for a cohesive 3x3 brand identity board spanning strategy-derived logo concept, palette, type, and digital/physical applications. It deliberately produces a presentation reference, not usable logo assets or UI screens.

nodes.name: brutalist.md
nodes.summary: Opt-in brutalist/industrial preset with high layout variance, mechanical motion, bimodal density, one committed substrate, and hard zero-radius/grid-line rules. It is explicitly unsafe as a style fallback when the brief is silent.

nodes.name: image-to-code.md
nodes.summary: Image-first implementation pipeline that generates one reference per section, extracts concrete design properties, and then translates them faithfully into code. Ambiguity triggers a new detail image rather than cropping or generic guesswork.

nodes.name: imagegen-mobile.md
nodes.summary: Image-only mobile comp workflow that locks one platform idiom and design bible across a logically connected screen flow. Phone framing, safe areas, readable type, and mobile-native hierarchy are non-negotiable.

nodes.name: imagegen-web.md
nodes.summary: Image-only web-comp workflow that generates one horizontal image per requested section while holding palette, type, CTA family, radius logic, and color grade consistent across the set. It supplies concrete default section counts and resists repeated template compositions.

nodes.name: minimal.md
nodes.summary: Editorial-minimal preset for calm working surfaces, using restrained dials, distinct sans/serif/mono roles, warm monochrome surfaces, small pastel accents, hairline borders, and nearly invisible motion.

nodes.name: redesign.md
nodes.summary: Audit-first workflow for improving an existing UI inside its current stack: inventory, set dials, diagnose against a fixed checklist, then apply independently shippable fixes in impact/risk order. It explicitly prohibits framework migration and rewrite-sized diffs.

nodes.name: soft.md
nodes.summary: Calm/premium style preset that biases toward whitespace, spring-like motion, and one committed glass, editorial-warm, or soft-structuralist archetype. It supplies nested shell/core components and rejects hard generic shadows and equal card grids.

nodes.name: stitch-DESIGN.md
nodes.summary: Fill-in design-spec template for one-shot screen generators, covering dial values, atmosphere, exact palette/type/layout/component choices, static versus deferred motion intent, and restated banned defaults. Every bracket must be resolved before handoff.

nodes.name: stitch.md
nodes.summary: Workflow for producing a concrete single-file design spec for one-shot static screen generators. It moves iterative checks into explicit values and separates what renders now from interaction/motion intent implemented later.

nodes.name: strict.md
nodes.summary: Verify-first variant that forces stable-but-varied layout/type/motion choices and a written preflight before code. The preflight proves headline wrapping, complete grid occupancy, real labels, and explicit composition decisions.

nodes.name: v1.md
nodes.summary: Fixed-baseline frontend preset for consistency across runs, starting at variance 8, motion 6, and density 4 unless the user explicitly redirects. It also bundles React/Next, CSS Grid, dynamic-viewport, and dependency-reuse conventions.

nodes.name: PATTERNS.md
nodes.summary: Reference catalog of orchestration mechanisms covering capability seams, hook pipelines, append-only state, guarded execution, bounded delegation and retries, asynchronous runs, trust boundaries, quality gates, and progressive disclosure.

nodes.name: MAP.md
nodes.summary: Initial placeholder project-map template that marks the map as not built and directs an agent to run the godkit-map workflow.

nodes.name: THREAD.md
nodes.summary: Append-only inter-agent message template for timestamped, attributed, task-linked actionable communication, including recipients and blockers.

nodes.name: cursor-header.md
nodes.summary: Cursor-rule frontmatter template that marks generated Godkit rules as always active with an empty glob filter and a shared-protocol description.

nodes.name: save.test.js
nodes.summary: CLI integration tests for graph save behavior, including graph/MAP/meta output, partial retention versus full replacement, corruption and missing-input refusal, tmp cleanup, path privacy, and freshness status.

nodes.name: session.js
nodes.summary: Host-neutral hook input and per-session runtime state. Session ids are hashed before they become path components and state lives only under a godkit-owned directory, so one session can never read or clear another. Also the atomic writer (temp + fsync + rename, optional compare-and-swap and .bak) that every config write in the package goes through.

nodes.name: readHookInput
nodes.summary: Reads and validates a hook payload from stdin; malformed input warns and yields {} rather than throwing, because a hook that throws breaks the session it exists to help.

nodes.name: statePath
nodes.summary: Resolves a state file path from namespace + session id. Rejects unknown namespaces, missing session ids and unsafe leaf names; the raw host id is hashed, never used as a path component.

nodes.name: atomicWriteFile
nodes.summary: Temp-and-rename write with fsync, optional expectedRaw compare-and-swap and optional .bak. The one write path for settings, config and map files.

nodes.name: clearSession
nodes.summary: Removes every namespace for one session. Refuses any cleanup target that resolves outside the owned state root.

nodes.name: work.js
nodes.summary: Session-owned evidence that a tool changed project files — the thing clockout judges. Shell tools compare a before/after Git fingerprint that excludes .agent/, edit tools mark work only for successful paths outside it. A dirty working tree is deliberately NOT evidence: it says nothing about which session made it.

nodes.name: fingerprint
nodes.summary: SHA-256 over the non-.agent tree plus working-tree status and content, so an .agent-only checkpoint does not count as product work while a source commit does.

nodes.name: statusPaths
nodes.summary: Parses git porcelain -z records into paths, consuming the second path of a rename or copy record. Shared with lib/freshness so neither invents a filename out of "old -> new".

nodes.name: recordDirectEdit
nodes.summary: Marks work for a successful Edit/Write/apply_patch/NotebookEdit whose target lands inside the project and outside .agent/.

nodes.name: didSessionWork
nodes.summary: The question clockout asks: did THIS session change project files?

nodes.name: managed.js
nodes.summary: A managed block is godkit's few lines inside a file the user also owns. init used to skip any host file that already existed, which silently meant "this project gets no rules"; overwriting would have eaten the user's text. Marked blocks do neither, and ambiguous or hand-edited markers are refused rather than guessed at.

nodes.name: applyBlock
nodes.summary: Creates, appends, updates or reports-unchanged the marked block, leaving every byte outside the markers alone.

nodes.name: locate
nodes.summary: Finds the single marker pair, throwing on a duplicate, unbalanced, or reversed pair.

nodes.name: freshness.js
nodes.summary: Is the map still true? staleness() is git-only and safe on every session start; classify() decides how much to rebuild. It fails CLOSED: an unreadable status, a meta sha the repo no longer has, or a failed diff all report unknown or stale — never fresh. A hook that blesses a map nobody verified is the one wrong answer.

nodes.name: staleness
nodes.summary: fresh | stale | unbuilt | unknown, from HEAD, the working tree, and whether meta.sha is still reachable.

nodes.name: classify
nodes.summary: SKIP | PARTIAL | ARCHITECTURE | FULL, from how many files moved and whether a new top-level directory appeared.

nodes.name: evolve.js
nodes.summary: Project skills in .agent/skills/: what they are, whether they are safe to project into a host path, and what the log stream says about each. Projections are owned SHA-256 snapshots, not live links, so godkit replaces only what it wrote and never removes a foreign target. Trust is derived from logs alone — there is no separate store.

nodes.name: frontmatter
nodes.summary: A deliberate YAML subset — quoted scalars, comments, block scalars, duplicate-key detection — reporting malformed metadata as blocking findings. Hand-rolled because zero runtime dependencies is a hard constraint.

nodes.name: scanSkill
nodes.summary: Blocks linking on symlinks, executable extensions, executable mode bits, executable magic bytes, credentials and instruction-override text.

nodes.name: ownership
nodes.summary: absent | ours-link | ours-copy | ours-snapshot | ours-stale | foreign, by marker plus tree hash.

nodes.name: linkProjectSkills
nodes.summary: Projects approved skills as owned snapshots, revoking a projection that becomes quarantined or mode-gated.

nodes.name: trustOf
nodes.summary: Trust from distinct verified sessions, demoted by a blaming Bugs bullet and reset when revised: moves.

nodes.name: work-track.js
nodes.summary: The lifecycle hook that feeds work evidence: pre captures a fingerprint, post compares, edit records a direct edit, end clears the session. Registered on PreToolUse, PostToolUse and SessionEnd — without it nothing records work and clockout can never fire.

nodes.name: install.js
nodes.summary: Standalone hook registration for a settings file: a thin CLI over lib/install.js with --uninstall and --dry-run. Paths derive from where this file actually lives, so moving the package is a re-run rather than a text hunt.

nodes.name: lazy-activate.js
nodes.summary: SessionStart hook that resolves the godkit-lazy mode for this session and injects its ruleset. Mode state is per session, under the owned state root.

nodes.name: lazy-subagent.js
nodes.summary: SubagentStart hook. Inherits the parent session's lazy rules; a malformed matcher fails closed and warns rather than broadening its own scope.

nodes.name: lazy-mode-tracker.js
nodes.summary: UserPromptSubmit hook tracking /godkit-lazy switches and deactivation for the session.

nodes.name: map-watch.js
nodes.summary: PostToolUse (Bash) hook. After a command that lands a change, says whether the map went stale — and stays quiet otherwise, because a warning that fires constantly gets muted.

nodes.name: godkit-hooks.json
nodes.summary: The plugin hook manifest read by Claude Code and Codex. GENERATED from the HOOKS list in lib/install.js by scripts/sync-hooks.js; CI fails if it drifted. It was hand-maintained until a hook was added to the settings installer and not to this file.

nodes.name: godkit-hooks.json
nodes.summary: Ten registrations across SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop and SessionEnd. Matchers are chosen to mean the same under Claude Code (literal or regex) and Codex (always regex).

nodes.name: uninstall.js
nodes.summary: Removes what a host's own uninstall cannot see: installed skill directories, hook registrations, and the session-state root. Shares every ownership decision with lib/install.js, so what install created is exactly what uninstall removes — nothing else.

nodes.name: removeSkills
nodes.summary: Per-tool removal through removeOne; a foreign directory is kept and reported.

nodes.name: removeHooks
nodes.summary: Strips our handlers from each settings file, leaving other tools' hooks — including ones sharing a group.

nodes.name: removeRuntimeState
nodes.summary: Clears the per-session state root. The persisted lazy default mode is user config and is left alone.

nodes.name: sync-hooks.js
nodes.summary: Generates hooks/godkit-hooks.json from the HOOKS list in lib/install.js; --check fails if it drifted. A generated manifest cannot disagree with the installer, which is exactly how work-track came to be missing from one of them.

nodes.name: check-versions.js
nodes.summary: Every version-bearing manifest must carry the same version, and on a tag push that version must equal the tag. An empty or non-release tag now fails instead of skipping the check — the case where skipping is most dangerous.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Compares four manifests, then the agreed version against GITHUB_REF_NAME when the ref is a tag.

nodes.name: gitattributes
nodes.summary: The -merge rules for the generated half of .agent/, shipped as a template because godkit init writes them into every project. They lived only in this repo's own .gitattributes, which npm does not ship, so init crashed from an installed package.

nodes.name: agent-portability.md
nodes.summary: What each host actually reads, and which of those claims are verified versus best-effort. The honesty convention matters more than the table: an unverified adapter is labelled, never presented as certain.

nodes.name: runtime.test.js
nodes.summary: The hook runtime boundaries: shared state resolves to the main worktree from a linked one, reads stay inside .agent/ and inside a byte budget, session state is isolated and cleanable, work evidence tracks the session, lazy mode belongs to one session.

nodes.name: hook-install.test.js
nodes.summary: Install idempotence and the ownership rule. The two bugs it exists for: matching our entries by package name (which matched nothing, so re-runs appended), and filtering whole groups (which took a user hook out with ours).

nodes.name: hooks.test.js
nodes.summary: Hooks never throw, never block a read-only session, and never loop. Clockout is asserted against recorded session work, not a dirty tree, and every hook runs against a temp CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR so no test writes real home config.

nodes.name: package.test.js
nodes.summary: Contract tests: the package ships what the README promises, manifests agree, generated files are current, and — the one that catches an allowlist bug — the packed file set can actually run godkit init from a temp directory.

nodes.name: evolve.test.js
nodes.summary: Project-skill snapshots, quarantine, frontmatter parsing, trust promotion and demotion, and fixture cleanup.

nodes.name: graph.test.js
nodes.summary: Graph portability and persistence: absolute ids rejected, last-wins edges, atomic write with rollback.

nodes.name: scan.test.js
nodes.summary: Scan, category, import resolution, batching, and the documented .agentignore subset.

nodes.name: test.yml
nodes.summary: Matrix CI across ubuntu and windows on Node 18, 22 and 24. Least-privilege token, cancels superseded runs, and caps each job at 10 minutes so a hook hung on stdin fails fast instead of burning six jobs for six hours. Windows is not optional: path handling and hook stdin differ there.

nodes.name: test
nodes.summary: push to main / PR / dispatch -> 6-way matrix -> sync-rules --check -> sync-hooks --check -> check-versions -> node --test.

nodes.name: publish.yml
nodes.summary: Tag-only publish. workflow_dispatch is deliberately absent: it could publish a branch the tag gate never examined. Serialised without cancel-in-progress, because interrupting a release half way is worse than running two in order.

nodes.name: publish
nodes.summary: tag v* -> generated-file and version checks (the version check also asserts the tag IS the manifest version) -> node --test -> npm pack --dry-run -> OIDC trusted publish with provenance.

nodes.name: hotspots.js
nodes.summary: Which code files the log stream says are hot: claimed in `scope:`, listed under `## Did`, or named as a root cause under `## Bugs`, cross-referenced against the map for fan-in. Reads no source code and scores no file the map does not know, so prose that merely looks like a path cannot rank. The deterministic half of godkit-refactor.

nodes.name: report
nodes.summary: Ranks code files by blamed x2 + touched over the whole log stream. Returns ok:false when there is no map — a silent empty table would read as a clean codebase.

nodes.name: filesIn
nodes.summary: Real files named anywhere in a blob of log prose, glob claims expanded. Every candidate is checked against the map, which is what decides whether a token is a file.

nodes.name: fanIn
nodes.summary: How many other files depend on each one, from the graph edges. Self-edges do not count.

nodes.name: hotspots.test.js
nodes.summary: The ranking contract: blame outranks a bare touch, a glob claim counts for every file it names and nothing outside its directory, path-shaped prose scores nothing, docs are ranked out, a missing map is reported rather than rendered as a clean codebase, and fan-in ignores self-edges.

nodes.name: godkit-refactor.toml
nodes.summary: Slash command for the godkit-refactor skill. One command per skill is a contract test.

nodes.name: CHANGELOG.md
nodes.summary: Release history. 1.0.0 is the first public release.

nodes.name: godkit.js
nodes.summary: The CLI, and the deterministic half of everything: init, install, hooks, scan, save, sprint, skills, evolve, refactor, verify, doctor, uninstall, --version. Every command that needs judgment stops at the point where judgment starts and hands off to a skill.

nodes.name: cmdInit
nodes.summary: Scaffolds .agent/ and writes the rules into managed blocks in AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and the Cursor/Codex rule files. --new is greenfield: writes .agent/BRIEF.md and skips the map entirely. Also runs the machine half (skills + hooks) unless --no-install, but ONLY when machineReady() is false.

nodes.name: machineReady
nodes.summary: Whether every tool that takes skills already has them and every hook is registered. This is what stops init from rewriting home config on every project: false once, true forever after. Added because unconditional writes raced on ~/.claude/settings.json (B-014).

nodes.name: cmdSprint
nodes.summary: new opens .agent/sprints/S-NNN.md from the template; no argument reports the current sprint and its tasks; close refuses while any named task is unfinished, unwritten, or done with an empty ## Test. Never invents tasks - cutting waves is the model's job.

nodes.name: cmdVerify
nodes.summary: Runs lib/contract over every task and log and exits non-zero on any finding. The rules were always in the templates; this is what finally reads them back.

nodes.name: cmdInstall
nodes.summary: Places the skills per tool through installOne, refusing any destination godkit does not own.

nodes.name: cmdHooks
nodes.summary: status | install | uninstall over the Claude and Codex settings files, with --dry-run.

nodes.name: cmdSave
nodes.summary: Load-patch-save of the map: replaces re-analyzed files, keeps untouched ones, drops nodes whose file no longer exists. Writes meta.json last so an interrupted run reads as stale.

nodes.name: cmdScan
nodes.summary: Deterministic walk, categorize, resolve imports and batch - the token-free half of the map.

nodes.name: cmdDoctor
nodes.summary: What is set up here: .agent files, map freshness (greenfield-aware), project skills, installed skills per tool, and the hook registrations. Prints the version first.

nodes.name: contract.js
nodes.summary: The rules godkit already wrote down, made checkable. .agent/tasks/ and .agent/log/ were write-only until this existed: a task could sit at done with nothing behind it. Structural only - present, non-empty, not the template placeholder. Whether evidence is any GOOD stays with godkit-review, deliberately, because a fuzzy check would train agents to write around it.

nodes.name: checkTask
nodes.summary: Empty scope or exit, a started task with no owner or a non-model owner, phase done with an empty ## Test, an unfinished task with an empty ## Handoff, blocked with no typed reason.

nodes.name: checkLog
nodes.summary: agent: must be a model id; status done needs ## Verified; partial or blocked needs ## Left / next. The clockout hook enforces exactly one of these (no-verify) and leaves the rest advisory, because a Stop hook that blocks on everything is a wall.

nodes.name: parseFrontmatter
nodes.summary: The frontmatter block only - a --- later in the body is content, not a delimiter. Every other module parses task and log frontmatter through this one, including lib/sprint.

nodes.name: identity.js
nodes.summary: Who wrote this, in the only terms that stay true: the model, not the tool it ran inside. 'claude' is four different models with four different failure modes, and a year from now it is four others. Deliberately NOT a registry of known ids - a shipped allowlist is wrong within a quarter and then rejects the truth, so this only refuses what is definitely not a model id and lets the model name itself.

nodes.name: looksLikeModelId
nodes.summary: Two or more '-' separated segments and a digit somewhere. claude-opus-5 and codex-5.6-terra pass; claude and cursor do not. 'unrecorded' also passes - it is the one honest value for an entry written before the rule, because back-filling a guess would fabricate attribution.

nodes.name: isPlatformName
nodes.summary: The blocklist of tool, vendor and role names that get typed where a model id belongs.

nodes.name: sprint.js
nodes.summary: A sprint is a goal plus waves of file-disjoint tasks. This does only the half a machine can do: find the sprints, resolve the task ids the wave table names, and say whether every one is finished with evidence behind it. Reuses lib/contract for the checking rather than growing a second frontmatter parser that would immediately disagree with the first.

nodes.name: blockers
nodes.summary: Why a sprint cannot close, as reasons rather than a boolean: a named task with no file, a task not yet done, or any contract finding on one. An empty sprint cannot close either.

nodes.name: meta
nodes.summary: Reads one sprint file. Task ids come out of the wave table text with HTML comments stripped first - the template ships a worked example inside <!-- -->, and reading its ids reported two tasks nobody wrote as missing on every fresh sprint (B-015).

nodes.name: current
nodes.summary: The newest OPEN sprint, falling back to the newest of any status. Ids are zero-padded so they sort lexically, which is the reason they are padded.

nodes.name: install.js
nodes.summary: What godkit owns on this machine, and nothing else. installOne refuses a destination it did not create; removeOne keeps what is not ours and says so. writeSettings is a temp-and-rename compared against the bytes it read, and is a NO-OP when the new body is byte-identical - without that, re-registering identical hooks renamed a file over the user's live config every time, which on Windows is an EPERM as soon as two processes land together (B-014).

nodes.name: paths.js
nodes.summary: Locating shared project state. .agent/ belongs to the MAIN worktree so it survives linked worktree removal, and every read below it is bounded and refuses symlinks - a project-controlled link must not turn a session brief into a local-file reader. One exported real() canonicalizer, because two spellings of one directory compared as different and made Windows CI red for a week (B-012). Now also carries brief and sprints paths.

nodes.name: brief.js
nodes.summary: SessionStart: injects a bounded view of the shared state - board, map freshness, project skills, the two newest logs, the thread tail. Every section has its own byte budget so a large BOARD cannot starve the rest. The closing reminder is the one sentence injected into EVERY session, so it carries only what cannot be dropped: claim your scope, sign with your model, write your log.

nodes.name: clockout.js
nodes.summary: Stop: a session that changed project files keeps blocking until its own exact-session log exists. Judges the session, not the directory - someone else's dirty file is not evidence about you. Enforces exactly one contract rule (a done log with an empty ## Verified); the filename it suggests carries a <your-model-id> placeholder rather than a guessed tool name.

nodes.name: BRIEF.md
nodes.summary: Stands in for MAP.md on a project with no code yet. Non-goals is the load-bearing section: on an empty repo it is the only thing stopping an agent from inventing scope.

nodes.name: sprint.md
nodes.summary: A goal and a wave table. The worked example is inside an HTML comment on purpose - a blank form teaches less than a filled one - which is exactly why lib/sprint strips comments before reading task ids.

nodes.name: BOARD.md
nodes.summary: One screen of current truth: roster, claims, task index, bugs, binding decisions, handoffs. The roster names MODELS with tools as a second column, because cost and capability belong to the model. Carries the current sprint id on one line.

nodes.name: log.md
nodes.summary: One log file per session - the reason two tools writing at once never conflict. agent: must be a model id. Its frontmatter is generated into godkit-handoff by scripts/sync-templates.js, so this file is the single source for the format.

nodes.name: task.md
nodes.summary: Plan, Execute, Review, Test, Handoff, with scope and a checkable exit in frontmatter. owner: is a model id once claimed. Same generated-into-the-skill arrangement as log.md.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: The product page, and what npmjs.com renders. Carries the install paths, the sprint loop, the model-identity rule, and the reference depth folded into <details>. Images use absolute raw URLs so they render on npm as well as GitHub.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Published as @codeforfee/godkit - the bare name is permanently refused by npm as too similar to the existing god-kit. Zero runtime dependencies, node >=18, and a files allowlist that is the real risk here: a runtime file missing from it works in a checkout and 404s for everyone who installed.

nodes.name: logo.svg
nodes.summary: Light-theme mark: four agents, one shared centre. Repo-only, never packed.

nodes.name: logo-dark.svg
nodes.summary: Dark-theme mark, referenced through <picture> in the README.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: The canonical always-on protocol every host reads, and the only copy worth editing - the Claude, Cursor, Codex and Copilot rule files are generated from it and byte-compared in CI. Now also states the model-identity rule, which is where that rule actually gets enforced on hosts with no hook support.

nodes.name: identity.test.js
nodes.summary: Pins the rule that a tool name is not an identity, across every vendor, plus the 'unrecorded' sentinel and the fact that why() never suggests it.

nodes.name: sprint.test.js
nodes.summary: Pins the refusals: a wave table naming a task nobody wrote, an unfinished task, a done task with no evidence, an empty sprint - and that the shipped template's commented example names no real tasks.

nodes.name: contract.test.js
nodes.summary: Every contract rule against the sentence that states it, including no-identity on tasks and logs and the fact that the shipped log template does not pass its own checks as done.

nodes.name: cli.test.js
nodes.summary: The CLI end to end in temp repos: managed blocks, init (plain and --new), freshness, hooks, sprint lifecycle, verify. Every init here passes --no-install, because a project-scaffolding test must never write to the real home directory.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: The arrival protocol and the sprint loop: read .agent/, refresh a stale map, cut seams on file boundaries, claim scope, run waves behind a join gate.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: The .agent/ file formats and the clock-in / clock-out checklists. Its task and log frontmatter blocks are GENERATED from templates/ by scripts/sync-templates.js - edit the template, not the skill.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Cutting a task into seams on file boundaries, each with scope, exit and verification, then writing them out and claiming one.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Building and refreshing this map. Says which of SKIP/PARTIAL/ARCHITECTURE/FULL to do, and why writing only fresh entries over the whole graph fails silently.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Worktrees as the backstop for a board claim, commit as checkpoint, and why .agent/ rarely conflicts.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: The five-stage pipeline, and retry only on verified advancement.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Two ladders - fewest turns, then least code. lib/lazy injects this whole body into every session AND every subagent, so its LENGTH is a per-session cost, not a per-trigger one. That is why it is kept short.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: What counts as verified, and the smallest check that fails if the logic breaks.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Ranking code files by churn and blame from the log stream, then reading them. Evolves SOURCE; godkit-evolve evolves procedures.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Locking a deliverable count so generated output is not handed over stubbed or truncated.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Design taste for UI work: three numeric dials set from the brief before any CSS, and a banned-defaults list for the look every unguided model converges on.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Reviewing how work was ORGANIZED, and diagnosing a run that went wrong. Never judges code correctness.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: GitHub issues and PRs: fresh-base diffs, the confidence x severity posting gate, batch clustering.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Pressure-testing a decision before it lands under Decisions and binds everyone after you.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: Capturing a repeated procedure into .agent/skills/, as an approved snapshot that is inert until linked.

nodes.name: SKILL.md
nodes.summary: The quick reference card.

nodes.name: motion.js
nodes.summary: Every GSAP scene, and the reason each one exists. Also the safety rule the page depends on: NOTHING is hidden by CSS, so a page whose JS never loads is the finished document. This module sets the from-state itself, immediately before animating it back.

nodes.name: +layout.js
nodes.summary: prerender + ssr + csr: the content is in the served HTML, and the client pass only layers motion on top of a page that already works.

nodes.name: app.html
nodes.summary: The document shell: title, description, canonical, OG tags, fonts.

nodes.name: svelte.config.js
nodes.summary: adapter-static, fully prerendered into build/ as plain files.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: The site's own project, deliberately separate from the CLI's: it has devDependencies and GSAP, and the root package must stay at zero. site/ is outside the root files allowlist, so none of this ever reaches the npm tarball.

nodes.name: vercel.json
nodes.summary: Build command, output directory and security headers for Vercel. Root Directory must be set to `site`.

nodes.name: +page.svelte
nodes.summary: The whole landing page: hero, the private-memory-vs-shared-state scene, the six-step session protocol, the .agent/ tree, sprint waves, model identity, hosts and the CLI. One file on purpose - it is one document.

layers.name: Shared protocol and state
layers.description: AGENTS.md and the committed .agent/ contract every host reads: board, thread, brief, sprints, tasks, logs, map. One canonical copy of each fact, with the host rule files generated from it.

layers.name: The contract - what counts as done
layers.description: The rules the templates state, made checkable, plus the identity rule that says a log is signed by a model and never by a tool. Structural only, on purpose: judging whether evidence is good stays with godkit-review.

layers.name: Work organisation - seams and sprints
layers.description: A task is one seam; a sprint is a goal plus waves of file-disjoint tasks behind a join gate. The CLI owns only what a machine can decide here; cutting the waves is the model's job.

layers.name: Session runtime
layers.description: Host-neutral primitives for hook input and per-session state, isolated by session id under a godkit-owned directory and replaced atomically.

layers.name: Hook enforcement
layers.description: Where the protocol stops being advice on Claude Code and Codex: the session brief in, the clock-out block on the way out. Hooks never throw.

layers.name: Install and ownership
layers.description: What godkit owns on a machine and nothing else. Refuses any destination it did not create, and does not rewrite a settings file that already says the right thing.

layers.name: CLI and the map pipeline
layers.description: The entry point, and the deterministic half of the map: walk, categorize, resolve imports, batch, then load-patch-save. The judgment half lives in agents/ and godkit-map.

layers.name: Skills and evidence
layers.description: The sixteen shipped skills, the project-local ones in .agent/skills/, and the trust derived from the log stream alone - a usage/outcome correlation, never a quality score.

layers.name: Release guards
layers.description: The generated files that cannot be edited in the wrong place, the version agreement across four manifests, and the pack check - a runtime file missing from the files allowlist works in a checkout and 404s for everyone else.

tour.title: AGENTS.md - the protocol itself
tour.description: Two rules, the clock-in/clock-out checklist, and the model-identity rule. Every other rule file in the repo is generated from this one, so it is the only copy worth reading or editing.

tour.title: bin/godkit.js - where execution begins
tour.description: One switch, one command per concern. Read cmdInit first: it is the whole install story, including why the machine half runs at most once.

tour.title: lib/contract.js - what 'done' has to mean
tour.description: The templates always stated the rules; nothing read them back until this. Structural checks only, and the reason that boundary is deliberate.

tour.title: lib/sprint.js - a goal, and waves that do not collide
tour.description: Note what it does NOT do: it never invents tasks. The machine resolves ids and checks evidence; cutting the waves is judgment and stays with the model.

tour.title: hooks/brief.js and hooks/clockout.js - the enforcement
tour.description: Where the protocol stops being advice. Brief injects the shared state on the way in under a strict byte budget; clockout blocks the turn on the way out if this session changed files and wrote no log.

tour.title: lib/paths.js - the safety floor everything stands on
tour.description: Bounded, symlink-refusing reads below .agent/, and one canonicalizer. Two spellings of one directory once made Windows CI red for a week.

tour.title: lib/install.js - owning only what you created
tour.description: Refuses a destination it did not write, and will not rewrite a settings file that already says the right thing. Both rules exist because of a real bug.

tour.title: package.json and scripts/ - the release guards
tour.description: Four manifests must agree on the version, four rule files are generated and byte-compared, and npm pack --dry-run is the only check that catches a runtime file missing from the allowlist.
